name: Taksh L0.5.1 Multilingual Coding Benchmark (starter)
status: SPECIFICATION ONLY - no model has been evaluated on it; execution harness ships with L1.0
provenance: Authored independently for Taksh L0.5.1 (2026-11). No problems are copied or paraphrased from any external benchmark. Python-family problems are distinct from the frozen L0.2 Python benchmark.

families.name: basic_programs
families.definition: simple functions demonstrating fundamental control flow and arithmetic

families.name: algorithms_and_data_structures
families.definition: loops, conditionals, arrays/lists, stacks/queues, searching and accumulation

families.name: strings_and_collections
families.definition: string manipulation, maps/dictionaries, set operations, formatting

families.name: error_handling
families.definition: edge cases, zero division, invalid input, empty collections, expected failure behaviour

families.name: file_and_data_processing
families.definition: read/transform/write records; temp-fixture based; no network

families.name: database_operations
families.definition: SQL-style schema manipulation and queries where relevant

families.name: api_and_application_development
families.definition: small multi-function application tasks (parsing, validation, routing)

families.name: debugging_and_error_correction
families.definition: given broken code, produce the corrected version

families.name: multi_file_project_tasks
families.definition: tasks spanning 2-4 files with cross-file references

scoring.unit_weight: each test assertion carries equal weight
scoring.consistency_requirement: 100% byte-identical outputs across repeated greedy runs

tasks.title: select_all_sales
tasks.statement: Given the table sales(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT NOT NULL, amount REAL NOT NULL), write a SQL query that returns all rows ordered by id ascending.

execution.note: dialect: SQLite; T-SQL/PL/SQL variants evaluate separately

tasks.title: total_amount_per_item
tasks.statement: Given the table sales(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT NOT NULL, amount REAL NOT NULL), write a SQL query that returns each item with the sum of its amounts, ordered by item ascending.

tasks.title: items_above_threshold
tasks.statement: Given the table sales(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT NOT NULL, amount REAL NOT NULL), write a SQL query that returns the item names whose amounts exceed 10, ordered by item ascending (duplicates allowed if multiple rows qualify).

tasks.title: empty_result_is_ok
tasks.statement: Given the table sales(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT NOT NULL, amount REAL NOT NULL), write a SQL query that returns rows where amount > 1e9. The correct answer is an empty result set (not an error).

tasks.title: divide_or_default

qualification.scoring: unit assertions, equal weight per assertion; a task passes only if all its assertions pass
qualification.status: PROPOSED, fixed before any model evaluation; never renegotiated after results
qualification.why: 4 starter tasks per language (64 total) cannot establish an 8-pass threshold; qualification requires a minimum task count per language

scoring_note: per-language success is the proportion of executed tasks that pass all unit assertions; languages below 16 executed tasks are NOT eligible for qualification regardless of pass ratio
